beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: What must remain open, portable, or independent for that benefit to survive?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Only then does the analysis examine the rules faced by potential sponsors.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Investors, public agencies, and regulators have different duties and different limits.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their refusals can be individually reasonable without providing a route for the project.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This reconstruction turns vague disappointment into a specific institutional question.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One recurring pattern requires evidence before funding or permission can be granted.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Yet producing that evidence may require the funding or permission already refused.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book calls this a proof trap and examines the surrounding accountability problem.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Public funders cannot simply accept every proposal that describes itself as visionary.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The issue is how uncertainty can be investigated without pretending it has vanished.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Bounded experiments and explicit responsibility offer alternatives the text asks readers to examine.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The detailed funding chapter separates checking facts from granting legitimate authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Public compute and verification infrastructure expose another version of the same problem.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their value can spread across many projects that no single owner controls.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Enclosing the foundation may create revenue while weakening the reason to build it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book compares ownership and payment arrangements fitted to that particular tension.
